about: The source patterns of 'building beside the engine', in ONE place. The lint tests (test/lint-foundations.test.ts, lint-costs.test.ts, lint-item-ops.test.ts) build their regexes from the entries that name them in `lint`; tools/built_from.py runs every entry on the ADDED lines of a diff and prints `instead` (looked up in docs/ENGINE-HOOKS.md). `re` is a regex source both JavaScript and Python read the same way. `scope`: a regex on the repo path the pattern applies to; `skip`: paths it never applies to (the primitive's own home). `kind`: 'zero' (the lint allows none: built_from fails), 'ratchet' (the lint counts them per file and the count only goes down: built_from fails when a file gains more than it lost), 'advisory' (no lint: a report only). Engine paths in `skip` are relative to packages/engine/src, as the lints read them.

bare_die.why: a bare die: d20 + a modifier against a number is a roll

log_raw.why: a line pushed on the fight log by hand (it skips the fog's marks)

pos_write.why: a unit put on a tile by hand (no Nailed, no knockback immunity, no forced_move hook, no trap)

ap_write.why: a unit's AP written by hand

round_compare.why: a round number kept by hand and compared with cb.round (a limit or a cooldown)

register_block.why: a new lane handler: an item that is 'when X, if Y, do Z, at most N' is data

handler_literal.why: a number typed in a handler (lint-item-ops counts them inside register blocks: the count only goes down)

hp_mp_write.why: HP or MP written by hand outside the damage and cost primitives

damage_math.why: damage or healing worked out by hand (the formula is effects/output.ts; a multiplier is data)

item_case.why: an item tested by its id in code (a handler by another name)

client_title.why: a hover text of its own on the client (every action's hover card is one helper)

client_number.why: a rule's number typed in a client file (the engine owns every number)

counter_field.why: a counter, round stamp or cooldown kept on a unit or the fight
